title: Verb to Be (am, is, are, was, were)

lessons.title: am, is, are in the Simple Present
lessons.content: The verb 'be' has three forms in the Simple Present tense: am, is, and are. Each form is used with specific subjects.

details.subject: I
details.burmese: ကျွန်မ ကျောင်းသားတစ်ယောက်ပါ။

details.subject: He/She/It
details.burmese: သူ ဆရာတစ်ယောက်ပါ။

details.subject: We/You/They
details.burmese: သူတို့ ဆရာဝန်တွေပါ။

lessons.title: was, were in the Simple Past
lessons.content: The verb 'be' has two forms in the Simple Past tense: was and were. 'Was' is used with I, he, she, it. 'Were' is used with we, you, they.

conjugation.subject: I
conjugation.example: I was at home last night.
conjugation.burmese: မနေ့ညက ကျွန်မ အိမ်မှာ ရှိခဲ့တယ်။

conjugation.subject: He
conjugation.example: He was a student two years ago.
conjugation.burmese: နှစ်နှစ်ကျော်က သူ ကျောင်းသားတစ်ယောက်ပါ။

conjugation.subject: She
conjugation.burmese: မနေ့ညက သူမ ပင်ပန်းနေတယ်။

conjugation.subject: It
conjugation.burmese: မနေ့က အအေးချမ်းတယ်။

conjugation.subject: You
conjugation.burmese: မနေ့က မင်း ပျော်ရွှင်ခဲ့တယ်။

conjugation.subject: They
conjugation.example: They were at the market last week.

lessons.title: Affirmative, Negative, Interrogative Sentences
lessons.content: We can form affirmative, negative, interrogative, and negative interrogative sentences using the verb 'be'.

lessons.title: Short Answers
lessons.content: When we are replying Yes/No Questions with 'be', we can use short or long form for the answer.

lessons.title: Subject and Verb-to-be Agreement
lessons.content: The form of 'be' must agree with the subject in number and person. I use am, he/she/it use is, we/you/they use are.
